This is too much. I would scale back most of these days to two or three of the things on your list.

Friday:  
Looks fine. Find a restaurant in the theater district to stay close to your hotel and take it easy after the long flight.

Saturday:  
Too much.  
Carnegie Hall is boring if you’re not seeing a show there. Jettison that.  
The Plaza is fun for lunch, if spendy. If you’re not eating there, it’s not really that interesting.  
Do Central Park. Go to Robert, the restaurant at the top of the Museum of Art & Design for lunch. It’s got good options for grown ups but also makes a decent burger for kids and a nice view of Central Park. Do FAO as you leave the park, then do Top of the Rock and the Christmas Tree FIRST before your other stores. See how much time/energy you have after that to do your stores. Radio City Music Hall isn’t very interesting if you’re not seeing a show there. Norma is a fine choice but a bit of a walk from your other options. Get pizza.

Sunday:  
You can literally spend a full day at the Museum of Natural History. Are you seeing a matinee or an evening show? If a matinee, I’d recommend moving the museum to a different day. Go to Grand Central this day, then take the 7 train to Bryant Park and SEE THE LIBRARY, which is incredible. Then get back on the 7 to go to Times Square and see your show! Rather than going to a steakhouse, which you can do anywhere in the US, go to a classic NYC diner like Ellen’s Stardust, which has singing waiters!

Monday:  
This is not a fun day for a kid. A lot of transit and not many activities. Go to the Museum of Natural History. Get tickets to the planetarium show. Take your time and get the most out of the museum. Leave in time for the cruise and Thai food.

Tuesday: Spyscape is a great idea. After Spyscape, if you have time, take the train down to Union Square and spend some time looking in the shops. Don’t miss The Strand bookshop, Forbidden Planet (a comic shop) or the costume shop! All fun for 10 year olds. Alternatively, this is a good time to do Lego, Nintendo, and Nike.

text:
Download the MTA TrainTime app on your phone. You can see when all the trains depart/arrive. If your partner’s cousin lives near the Ronkonkoma train line, trains run at least once every hour all night after midnight, every night, from Penn Station even on Sundays. On the Babylon (South Shore) line it skips an hour after midnight on Sundays (12:44, then 2:30, then 4:28 am). There are other lines but these lines are well traveled. 

Sunday is the slowest night in the city and trains. On Friday and Saturday nights, every train line runs more trains more often for people living on LI who want to party late in the city. Hope this info helps you decide which nights to stay in Manhattan vs Long Island.

It’s always a drag to commute, but hotels in Manhattan aren’t cheap. I would definitely think about staying on LI on the weekend nights when the trains are running more frequently and with more people. I’ve never felt Penn Station or the LIRR trains were unsafe, but a few times switching trains late at night at the Jamaica station I’ve felt a bit nervous before. Whenever possible, take trains that go straight through without having to switch trains.

Another important thing is, without a hotel room in Manhattan, you won’t have anywhere to go to just take a load off/break, have a little nap, change clothes or shower, etc.

Whatever you decide, I’m sure you’ll have a blast!!!
label: informative

text:
1) The daily LIRR transportation prices will probably be what we locals pay per week, per person. 2) That and if you miss the LIRR/suburban lines, you typically have to wait much much longer, and some lines don’t even run at night/off-peak so you risk getting stranded. 3) The daily time commitment is hefty. 

NY State transportation system (like LIRR) is different, suburban based, and more expensive, from the NY City transportation system (OMNY) which is cheaper, local, city based. So if you have to additionally use the LIRR/suburban line. you’ll pay much, much, more per day for transportation to commute to/from the NYS suburbs, and the prices additionally add up since you’ll need to pay for both local city transportation, and suburban transportation so it adds up. 

Local OMNY-NYC transportation has a weekly cap on fares I think it’s $36 max per person after which all rides are free (12 rides x$3 each) so that’s more economical. 

Get a cheap hotel within a few miles of the city center and you’ll be fine. You’ll likely spend little time in a hotel when visiting and touring.
